docs.title: Required fields for new experiments
docs.text:
Every formal experiment must record:

  • a falsifiable question or comparison;
  • exact input session identifiers and dataset version;
  • configuration, model/weights identifier, seed where relevant, and code revision;
  • machine, interpreter, library versions, and runtime conditions;
  • quantitative results and representative successes and failures;
  • invalid or interrupted measurements;
  • a conclusion limited to what the annotation protocol supports; and
  • paths to machine-readable and human-readable outputs.

docs.title: FTS ground-truth annotation protocol
docs.text: Dataset pilot: fts-pilot-v0.1 Object class: fts Annotation geometry: one axis-aligned bounding box per visible FTS Storage format: Ultralytics YOLO detection labels plus a CSV audit manifest Protocol status: fts-ground-truth-v1 frozen; 66 positives and 12 negatives verified

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
This protocol defines how the fischertechnik transport system (FTS) is sampled, annotated, reviewed, and split for detector evaluation. Its purpose is to make labels consistent enough to support a scientific comparison. It does not assume that the current YOLOE + CSRT baseline is correct.

The first 48-frame pilot validates the instructions and exposes ambiguous cases. It is too small to support a final accuracy claim or detector selection.

docs.title: 2. Annotation target
docs.text: Annotate the complete mobile FTS carrier as class fts (class_id = 0). The workpiece colour is incidental and must not create a separate class. Do not annotate fixed stations, chargers, rails, trays, workpieces, or other machinery as the FTS.

docs.title: Include
docs.text:
• the visible mobile carrier body;
  • attached structural parts that move rigidly with the carrier; and
  • the carried tray only when it is structurally part of the carrier silhouette.

docs.title: Exclude
docs.text:
• the coloured workpiece when it projects beyond the carrier body;
  • shadows, reflections, motion trails, and background objects;
  • fixed station structures, even when their shape resembles the FTS; and
  • guessed regions when no part of the FTS is visible.

docs.title: 3. Bounding-box rule
docs.text:
Draw the smallest axis-aligned rectangle enclosing all visible FTS pixels. Do not infer the full hidden size through a station or occluder. A box should be tight without cutting visible parts; a small margin of at most two pixels is acceptable when the boundary is anti-aliased or blurred.

When motion blur is present, include the solid visible object but exclude faint motion trails. When the FTS touches an image boundary, clip the box to the image.

docs.title: 4. Visibility decision
docs.text:
Assign exactly one visibility value in the manifest:

Value Rule clear At least 80% of the carrier is visible and its boundary is identifiable. partial Between 30% and 80% is visible, or a station hides part of the carrier. minimal Less than 30% is visible but the FTS identity and a defensible visible-region box remain clear. absent No FTS pixels are visible. The YOLO label file must exist and be empty. ambiguous The reviewer cannot distinguish the FTS from the scene confidently. Do not use the frame for model evaluation until resolved.

For minimal, record a box only when the visible pixels are confidently the FTS. Otherwise use ambiguous rather than inventing a box.

docs.title: 5. Difficulty tags
docs.text:
Assign one or more semicolon-separated tags after inspecting the image:

  • clear_view;
  • motion_blur;
  • partial_occlusion;
  • station_overlap;
  • turn_or_unusual_pose;
  • difficult_lighting;
  • image_edge;
  • small_scale;
  • station_only_negative;
  • empty_scene_negative; or
  • other:<short explanation>.

Sampling timestamps do not prove a difficulty category. Tags must be assigned by visual review, not automatically inferred from time or the baseline prediction.

docs.title: 6. Positive, negative, and rejected frames
docs.text:
• A positive frame has one defensible FTS box and a non-empty YOLO label.
  • A negative frame has visibility absent and an intentionally empty YOLO label file. Fixed stations should be represented among the negatives because they caused the dominant baseline failure.
  • An ambiguous frame is retained for discussion but excluded from training and evaluation until resolved.
  • A technically invalid frame (decode error, corruption, wrong source, or severe unusable blur) receives review status rejected with a reason.

An absent label file means not annotated yet. It must never be interpreted as a negative example. An empty existing label file means verified negative.

docs.title: 7. YOLO label format
docs.text:
Each positive image has a text file with one row:

0 x_center_normalized y_center_normalized width_normalized height_normalized

All four coordinates must be in [0, 1]. Coordinates describe the reviewed pixel box, normalized by the original image width and height. The current videos contain one FTS; a frame with more than one apparent carrier must be marked ambiguous and discussed before use.

docs.title: 8. Pilot sampling and split
docs.text:
The deterministic sampler extracts eight evenly distributed timestamps from each of the six recordings, for 48 candidate frames. Even spacing provides coverage across each route but does not guarantee every required visual condition. After the contact sheets are reviewed, additional targeted frames must be added for missing conditions—especially fixed-station negatives, occlusion, motion blur, turns, and difficult lighting.

The pilot uses a source-video split:

Split Source videos Purpose train od_red_1, od_blue_1, od_white_1 Develop annotation and detector settings val od_red_2 Select settings without using test evidence test od_blue_2, od_white_2 Final held-out pilot check

No frame from a validation or test video may be copied into training. If the split changes, create a new dataset version; do not silently edit the manifest. The final dataset must document the limitation that only six source recordings are available and report results by source video.

docs.title: 9. Annotation workflow
docs.text:
1. Run the dashboard and open FTS annotation in the left navigation.
  2. Enter the annotator’s name or initials once.
  3. For each image, drag one rectangle around the FTS or choose No FTS.
  4. Choose Unsure instead of guessing when the FTS cannot be identified.
  5. Record visibility, optional difficulty tags, and a note only when useful.
  6. Select Save & show next image. The interface writes the YOLO label, append-only decision, and manifest status automatically.
  7. Mark an item annotated only after checking box tightness and class identity.
  8. Finish every first-pass decision in the project before starting second review.
  9. A second review is mandatory for every validation and test item.
  10. Mark validation/test items verified only after that review.
  11. Resolve disagreements from the image itself, not from detector predictions.

docs.title: Validation/test second review
docs.text:
After the complete project first pass, select Start validation/test second review. For fts-pilot-v0.1, the queue contains only the 8 validation and 16 test frames. Recheck the saved answer and any cyan box, identify the reviewer, and choose exactly one action:

  • Approve saved label when class, visible extent, and metadata are correct;
  • Save corrected answer after changing an incorrect class/visibility answer or redrawing incorrect geometry; or
  • Flag as unsure when the evidence cannot support approval or correction.

Second reviews are append-only and separate from first-pass decisions. A correction replaces the authoritative YOLO label: a corrected positive writes the reviewed box, a corrected negative writes an empty label, and an ambiguous or rejected correction removes the label. The record retains both the first annotator and reviewer. Approval never silently changes the first-pass answer. A flagged frame is not verified and must be resolved before evaluation.

The original JPEG is never painted or modified. The visible cyan rectangle is a browser overlay; only its pixel coordinates are saved.

The current detector output may be displayed as a separate diagnostic overlay, but it must not be accepted as ground truth without manual placement and review.

docs.title: AI-assisted proposals
docs.text:
An AI-assisted box is an unverified proposal, not an annotation. The interface displays proposals in orange and excludes them from completion counts, YOLO labels, and evaluation. A human reviewer must choose one action:

  • Accept proposal: confirm the suggested class and box unchanged;
  • Adjust box: replace or redraw the suggested geometry;
  • Reject proposal: remove it and provide a new answer; or
  • Unsure: retain the frame for discussion instead of guessing.

After the reviewer explicitly saves, the decision becomes human-verified ground truth and records the proposal method plus whether it was accepted, adjusted, or rejected. The first five proposals form a calibration pilot. Their human review must be inspected before AI proposals are created for the remaining frames.

docs.title: Targeted negative-candidate review
docs.text:
The separate fts-negative-candidates-v0.1 project contains two pending frames from each source recording. Candidate timestamps preferentially come from the latest manually reviewed baseline detector errors, with recording-endpoint fallbacks where a source has fewer than two distinct error timestamps. This selection targets station confusers; it does not establish FTS absence.

Inspect the complete image in the ordinary first-pass workflow:

  • choose No FTS only when no FTS pixels are visible anywhere in the frame;
  • draw a normal FTS box when the detector was wrong but the FTS remains visible;
  • choose Unsure rather than manufacturing either a positive or negative;
  • assign station_only_negative or empty_scene_negative only after visual verification; and
  • second-review every validation and test decision before dataset freeze.

Extraction creates image files and pending manifest rows, but deliberately creates no label files. A human No FTS decision is the only operation that may create an empty YOLO label.

docs.title: Declared-empty source verification
docs.text:
The fts-verified-negatives-v0.1 project samples two new close-plan recordings:

  • cluttered empty operational view: 6 training candidates; and
  • clean empty operational view: 6 held-out test candidates.

The complete source recordings remain split-disjoint. Filenames and recording intent are selection evidence, not labels. Every sampled image requires the same whole-frame decision as a targeted candidate. A human No FTS save creates the empty label; the six test decisions then require second review before they can enter evaluation.

The wide-plan empty recording changes camera geometry and is reserved as an out-of-distribution stress source. It must not be mixed into the calibrated core dataset. New low-light route recordings and the cluttered CHRG recording are retained as future robustness evidence; they do not replace the missing core negative verification.

docs.title: Declared-empty result and frozen version
docs.text:
All 12 close-plan candidates were manually verified as No FTS. The six test decisions passed the mandatory second review. The combined fts-ground-truth-v1 freeze contains 78 frames: 66 positives and 12 negatives, split into 42 train, 10 validation, and 26 test frames. The freezer verified image checksums, class-0/empty-label consistency, held-out review completion, duplicate absence, and source-video isolation. Its deterministic freeze SHA-256 is 31b68230c3dfea649ee14dae591f4a24485f68f8a787f2f13c4f4df73c95100b.

The first annotator also performed every held-out second review. These checks are valid documented quality control under this protocol, but they must not be described as independent inter-annotator verification.

docs.title: 10. Quality checks
docs.text:
Before a dataset version is frozen, verify that:

  • every manifest row points to the expected source video, timestamp, and frame;
  • image checksums and dimensions are recorded;
  • every clear, partial, or minimal row has exactly one valid class-0 box;
  • every absent row has an existing empty label file;
  • no pending, ambiguous, or rejected row enters evaluation;
  • every validation and test row has reviewer name and review status verified;
  • each video contributes useful positive and difficult or negative evidence;
  • train, validation, and test source videos remain disjoint; and
  • a contact-sheet spot check shows no systematic loose boxes or station labels.

docs.title: 11. Pilot acceptance decision
docs.text:
After all 48 candidates are inspected, record:

  • the number of positive, negative, ambiguous, and rejected frames per video;
  • the represented difficulty conditions and missing conditions;
  • annotation-rule disagreements and their resolution;
  • whether the split remains suitable; and
  • the exact targeted frames needed before freezing fts-ground-truth-v1.

Only then should full annotation continue. Detector comparison begins after the versioned dataset passes the Milestone 2 acceptance gate.

docs.title: FTS detector evaluation contract v1
docs.text: Status: active development contract; test split sealed Dataset: fts-ground-truth-v1 Freeze SHA-256: 31b68230c3dfea649ee14dae591f4a24485f68f8a787f2f13c4f4df73c95100b Runtime target: CPU

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This contract prevents detector selection from adapting to the held-out test images. It applies to the YOLOE visual-prompt candidate and the lightweight one-class supervised candidate. Both methods must use the same frozen images, matching rule, metrics, and runtime measurement procedure.

docs.title: Evidence partitions
docs.text:
Phase Permitted evidence Prohibited use Development 42 train frames Final accuracy claim Selection 10 validation frames Reading test labels or selecting from test results Final comparison 26 test frames Any further threshold, prompt, constraint, hyperparameter, or checkpoint change

The complete source recording remains assigned to one partition. Frames must not be copied across partitions. Before every run, the dataset freeze hash must match the value above.

docs.title: Candidate A — YOLOE visual prompting
docs.text: Development may compare a small declared set of FTS reference views from training sources. Reference image, reference box, model checkpoint, image size, confidence threshold, and candidate constraints are selected only from training and validation evidence. The final configuration is written to an immutable run record before test inference.

docs.title: Candidate B — one-class supervised detector
docs.text:
Training uses only the 42 training images. Epoch count, augmentation, architecture, image size, and confidence threshold are selected using the 10 validation images. The exact checkpoint SHA-256 and inference configuration are recorded before test inference. Test images are not used for early stopping or checkpoint selection.

The initial candidate should be a lightweight Ultralytics detection model that can run on the target CPU. Architecture choice must be confirmed from installed Ultralytics support and measured locally rather than inferred from published GPU benchmarks.

docs.title: Matching and metrics
docs.text:
The task has one class, fts, and at most one verified FTS per frame. A prediction is a true positive when its xyxy box has intersection-over-union of at least 0.50 with the ground-truth box. A ground-truth box can match only one prediction. Additional predictions are false positives. An unmatched positive is a false negative; any prediction on a verified negative is a false positive.

Primary metrics:

  • precision;
  • recall; and
  • F1.

Secondary evidence:

  • AP50;
  • mean IoU among true positives;
  • number of false-positive frames and false negatives;
  • per-frame detection records;
  • mean and 95th-percentile inference latency; and
  • effective inference FPS.

Metrics are computed by tracktrace.evaluate. Confidence thresholds are chosen on validation data and then held fixed. Results must include raw integer counts, not only ratios.

docs.title: CPU timing procedure
docs.text: Load the model before timing, process three untimed warm-up images, then time each image with the same image size and device setting. Report mean and 95th-percentile latency and effective FPS. Model loading, file decoding, and visualization are excluded from inference latency and may be reported separately. The machine, Python, PyTorch, Ultralytics, and OpenCV versions must be captured in the run record.

docs.title: Test release gate
docs.text:
The test split may be opened exactly once for the primary comparison after:

  1. the YOLOE reference set and all inference constraints are locked;
  2. the supervised checkpoint and confidence threshold are locked;
  3. validation predictions and metrics are stored for both candidates; and
  4. both run records identify this contract and the frozen dataset hash.

After test release, poor results are findings—not permission to retune and report on the same test set. Any later method change requires a new held-out dataset version or must be labelled exploratory.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• The dataset has only 78 frames and 12 negatives.
  • The 12 negatives come from two deliberately empty close-plan recordings.
  • The first annotator also performed all held-out second reviews; this is not independent inter-annotator verification.
  • The wide-plan source is excluded from the core comparison and reserved for a separately labelled camera-geometry stress test.

docs.title: Validation selection record — 2026-07-31
docs.text:
Four YOLOE prompts were declared from od_red_1 training boxes before validation inference. The selected center-transit prompt produced 10 TP, 0 FP, and 0 FN on the 10 positive validation frames: precision, recall, F1, and AP50 were all 1.000, mean matched IoU was 0.798, and mean CPU inference was 178.0 ms.

The first supervised candidate used YOLO11n, seed 31, image size 640, and the declared train-only development view. Early stopping completed 40 of 100 planned epochs and selected epoch 20. Ultralytics' best-epoch validation metrics were precision 0.99365, recall 1.000, mAP50 0.995, and mAP50–95 0.8685. Under this contract's frame evaluator, confidence 0.05 produced 10 TP, 0 FP, and 0 FN: precision, recall, F1, and AP50 were all 1.000; mean matched IoU was 0.916; mean/p95 CPU inference was 50.4/53.1 ms (19.85 FPS).

These validation results establish positive-frame localisation only. The validation split has no verified negative frames, so its precision value cannot establish empty-scene rejection. That question remains sealed in the final test comparison.

docs.title: Locked final comparison — 2026-07-31
docs.text:
Both candidates were locked before test access, including artifact hashes, runtime parameters, validation metrics, and software versions. The 26-frame test was then released exactly once; it contains 20 positive and six verified empty frames.

Candidate TP FP FN Precision Recall F1 AP50 Mean IoU Mean CPU FPS YOLOE prompt 15 11 5 0.577 0.750 0.652 0.594 0.779 179.4 ms 5.57 YOLO11n 20 0 0 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 0.890 59.6 ms 16.77

YOLOE rejected none of the six empty frames; supervised YOLO11n rejected all six. supervised-yolo11n-v1 is therefore selected under the predeclared F1-first rule and is approximately 3.0 times faster by mean CPU inference. No post-test tuning was performed. This conclusion is limited to still-frame detection; tracking, low-light, camera-geometry shift, and production behavior remain separate experiments.

docs.title: FTS annotation pilot — v0.1
docs.text: Prepared: 2026-07-28 Status: 60 positive frames verified; no full-frame negative captured Purpose: validate the annotation protocol and identify missing visual conditions before freezing the first ground-truth dataset.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Can a small deterministic sample from all six recordings support a consistent one-class FTS annotation workflow, and which required visual conditions remain underrepresented?

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
The pilot sampler read the source metadata from the fixed 2026-07-27 baseline configuration. It selected eight evenly distributed interior timestamps from each recording and decoded the corresponding original-resolution frame. This produced 48 candidate images and one contact sheet per video.

The source-video split was fixed before annotation:

Split Videos Frames Train od_red_1, od_blue_1, od_white_1 24 Validation od_red_2 8 Test od_blue_2, od_white_2 16

Each manifest row records dataset version, source video, timestamp, source frame index, split, image dimensions, image checksum, and the expected annotation path. The annotation and review fields begin as pending.

No YOLO label files were created automatically. This is deliberate: a missing label means that the frame has not been annotated, while an existing empty label will mean that a human reviewer verified the frame as a negative example.

docs.title: Initial visual triage
docs.text:
Inspection of the six contact sheets shows:

  • open-floor FTS positions in several parts of the route;
  • views in which the FTS overlaps or is partly hidden by a station;
  • station-dominated scenes relevant to the known false-lock problem; and
  • diagonal or turning poses, particularly in the later od_white_2 samples.

This triage is not an annotation result. It does not establish the number of positive or negative frames and does not provide detector accuracy.

docs.title: AI-assisted calibration pilot — 2026-07-29
docs.text:
Five images from different source videos and dataset splits received visual AI box proposals. The sample includes a clear station-adjacent view, station overlap and partial occlusion, an image-edge case, and two blurred diagonal poses. All proposals have medium qualitative confidence.

The proposals are stored separately from human decisions. They do not create YOLO labels and do not increase annotation progress. In the dashboard, orange boxes mean “awaiting human verification.” A reviewer can accept, adjust, reject, or mark the image unsure. Only an explicit human save creates ground truth.

This five-image review tests whether visual AI assistance is useful for the specific FTS appearance. The remaining 43 frames must not receive automatic proposals until the pilot boxes and class decisions have been checked.

docs.title: Human review result
docs.text:
The reviewer completed all five AI proposals on 2026-07-29. Every proposal was saved as adjusted, rather than accepted unchanged. This result confirms that the initial visual proposals were not sufficiently localized for direct use. The corrected human boxes and proposal provenance remain stored in the append-only annotation decisions; the original images remain unchanged.

The IoU between each original proposal and its corrected box was 0.31, 0.47, 0.46, 0.00, and 0.44 respectively (mean 0.34). One proposal missed the corrected object entirely. These five corrected boxes are ground-truth candidates for the pilot and training examples for improving a future proposal method; the small sample is not sufficient to train or validate a detector by itself.

docs.title: First-pass completion — 2026-07-29
docs.text:
The first annotation pass is complete: 48/48 manifest frames have a saved human decision and 48 corresponding YOLO label files. An integrity audit found no missing images, decisions, labels, empty positive labels, or invalid boxes.

All 48 frames were labelled fts_visible: 46 clear and 2 partial. The split contains 24/24 annotated train frames, 8/8 validation frames, and 16/16 test frames. The append-only history contains 50 rows for 48 latest decisions because two frames were corrected and saved more than once; only the latest decision per frame is authoritative.

This completed the first pass, not dataset verification. The deterministic pilot contains no verified negative examples, so targeted station-only and empty-scene negatives must be added before detector evaluation claims are made.

docs.title: Validation/test quality check — 2026-07-29
docs.text:
All 24 held-out labels received a second pass: 8 validation and 16 test. The reviewer approved all 24 saved labels without a correction or uncertainty flag. An audit found 24 unique review records, verified manifest states, and zero missing authoritative labels.

Daniel Wonkam performed both the first pass and this second pass. This is therefore a same-reviewer quality check, not independent inter-annotator verification. The dataset must preserve that limitation in future evaluation reports. An independent reviewer would strengthen label-quality evidence if one becomes available.

docs.title: Targeted negative-candidate project — 2026-07-29
docs.text:
The deterministic fts-negative-candidates-v0.1 project initially contained 12 pending frames: two from each recording. Its source-video split is 6 train, 2 validation, and 4 test frames. Eleven timestamps come from the latest reviewed baseline detector errors and one is an explicit recording-endpoint fallback.

The pre-annotation artifact audit confirmed 12 readable 1920×1080 JPEGs, 12 recorded SHA-256 checksums, 12 distinct frame identifiers, and zero label or annotation-decision files. The contact sheet is consistent with the intended station-confuser and open-floor sampling, but visual triage is not a label. Every image remains a candidate, not a verified negative, until a human inspects the whole frame.

The dashboard displays this warning and selection evidence separately from editable annotator notes. It also keeps second review disabled until all 12 first-pass decisions are saved. After that pass, the 2 validation and 4 test decisions require quality review before dataset freeze.

docs.title: Human review result
docs.text:
The first pass and held-out quality review are complete. All 12 candidates were classified fts_visible with clear visibility; all 12 labels are non-empty. The 2 validation and 4 test decisions were approved without correction or an uncertainty flag. The append-only history contains 15 first-pass rows for 12 latest decisions and 6 review rows. A final audit found no missing decisions, reviews, labels, images, checksum mismatches, or invalid class-0 coordinates.

This is a scientifically useful negative result for the sampling hypothesis: reviewed detector errors locate station confusers, but they do not locate full-frame FTS absence. The fixed stations still contribute background evidence inside these positive images, yet the project added zero verified empty labels. Together, the two projects now contain 60 positives and 0 full-frame negatives.

docs.title: CHRG-positive supplement — 2026-07-29
docs.text:
The existing 66.133-second, 1920×1080, 30 FPS recording live_shopfloor_20260722_103616/camera.mp4 was inspected after the original pilot was found to lack CHRG examples. The FTS is parked at the charging station before a later manual relocation into the route. Six deterministic interior frames at 4.300, 8.567, 12.867, 17.133, 21.433, and 25.700 seconds were extracted as fts-chrg-supplement-v0.1.

All six frames belong to the training split because the complete source contains manual hand placement and must not become held-out evaluation evidence. The selected interval precedes that relocation. Human annotation is complete: all six frames are fts_visible with clear visibility, all six labels are non-empty, and five decisions carry the station_overlap difficulty tag. The append-only history contains nine rows for six latest decisions. A final audit found no missing decisions or labels, image/checksum failures, or invalid class-0 coordinates. The verified pool therefore contains 66 positives and 0 full-frame negatives.

docs.title: Limitations found
docs.text:
Uniform temporal sampling gives repeatable route coverage, but it does not ensure that every required condition is present. The contact sheets do not yet establish adequate coverage of:

  • verified empty scenes where no FTS pixels are visible;
  • strong motion blur;
  • difficult lighting; or
  • every degree of partial visibility.

The six available route recordings have not yielded a frame with whole-image FTS absence. A short empty-shopfloor recording, made with the same camera and calibration while the FTS is physically outside the field of view, is now the cleanest way to add true negatives. The pilot is therefore not yet fts-ground-truth-v1 and must not be used for a final detector comparison.

docs.title: Reproduction
docs.text:
Run the preparation script with the project interpreter:

& .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scripts.prepare_fts_annotation_pilot

The local output is stored under data/annotations/fts-pilot-v0.1/. Raw images and labels remain excluded from Git because they derive from private shopfloor recordings. The tracked protocol and this evidence summary preserve the scientific method without publishing the media.

docs.title: Next acceptance action
docs.text:
This action was completed on 2026-07-31. Two same-camera close-plan empty recordings produced 12 human-verified negative frames: six cluttered training examples and six clean held-out test examples. The test examples passed second review. The resulting fts-ground-truth-v1 contains 78 frames (66 positive, 12 negative), has no detected source split leakage, and has deterministic freeze SHA-256 31b68230c3dfea649ee14dae591f4a24485f68f8a787f2f13c4f4df73c95100b.

The same person performed first annotation and held-out review, so this is a documented same-reviewer check rather than independent inter-annotator verification. The next acceptance action belongs to Milestone 3: define the fixed detector-evaluation contract before tuning or training.

docs.title: Reconstructed project history
docs.text: This history was reconstructed from Git commits, dated data-session directories, experiment metadata, current code, and written project records. Dates marked recorded are supported directly by those artifacts. Where an exact date is not available, the text avoids inventing one.

docs.title: 2026-07-13 — Initial repository and thesis architecture
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by Git commit 46fdb38.

The project established its repository structure, quality criteria, Python package, tests, dashboard area, documentation folders, and a layered target architecture: capture, detection, tracking, zone mapping, interpretation, storage, evaluation, and dashboard. The safety boundary was observation only; the AI was not to control the shopfloor.

The initial plan mentioned Streamlit, YOLO, ByteTrack/BoT-SORT, and SQLite. These were planning choices rather than final implementation facts.

docs.title: 2026-07-20 — First hybrid tracking prototype
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by Git commit 3e47e72 and experiment folders.

A rapid hybrid method was added for the FTS and red and white workpieces. The FTS prototype combined YOLOE visual-prompt detection with CSRT tracking. This choice made it possible to test an object-specific detector without first labelling and training a dataset. Classical colour/motion methods supported workpiece exploration on the CPU-only development machine.

This stage demonstrated feasibility but did not yet provide a fixed experiment configuration or held-out accuracy measurement.

docs.title: 2026-07-21 — Live camera pipeline and latency investigation
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by dated live-session directories and current live modules/tests.

Camera smoke tests progressed to live shopfloor sessions. The main engineering problem was temporal latency: processing queued frames or moving preview images through disk made the displayed view stale. The pipeline moved toward a dedicated capture loop, latest-frame-only buffering, and separation of preview publication from slower inference. Dynamic camera discovery was introduced so connected cameras could be selected rather than assumed by a hard-coded index.

docs.title: 2026-07-22 — Repeated shopfloor validation
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by multiple dated live-session directories.

The live pipeline was exercised repeatedly under shopfloor conditions. These sessions provided engineering evidence for camera handling and runtime behaviour, but they were not labelled accuracy experiments. They should therefore not be used to claim detector precision or tracking accuracy.

docs.title: 2026-07-21 to 2026-07-27 — Dashboard architecture changed
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by current implementation, tests, README, and the legacy-plan warning in the backlog; exact change date is bounded but not committed separately.

The planned Streamlit dashboard was replaced by FastAPI and plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript. WebSocket carries live state and events, MJPEG carries the annotated image stream, and REST endpoints control sessions, camera discovery, replay, deletion, and review. This architecture was selected because direct streaming and independently updating channels fit real-time behaviour better than full-script reruns.

Session replay retained a compact dropdown, and individual recorded sessions could be deleted through explicit red delete controls with protected path handling.

docs.title: 2026-07-27 — Formal FTS baseline
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by commit 747d198, baseline configuration, metrics, and summary.

A sequential FTS roadmap was introduced to prevent further ad hoc tuning. The unchanged YOLOE + CSRT method was run on all six 1920×1080, 30 FPS recordings: two red, two blue, and two white sessions. The baseline fixed the reference, stride, redetection interval, confidence setting, image size, CPU device, zone map, and spatial constraints.

The automated result reported 99.8–100.0% output coverage and four suspicious jumps. Five uninterrupted runs processed approximately 14–23 source FPS. The od_blue_2 runtime was rejected as a performance benchmark because computer sleep contaminated wall-clock time.

The key methodological limitation was recognised: output continuity showed only that some box was emitted, not that the box represented the FTS.

docs.title: 2026-07-27 to 2026-07-28 — Human-review workflow
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by dashboard code, review log, report, and tests.

A dedicated FTS review workspace was added to the FastAPI dashboard. It presented every periodic detector lock, suspicious jump, and no-output gap, allowed nearby frame inspection, and stored structured decisions in an append-only JSONL log. Saving a newer row corrected a verdict without deleting history.

A reproducible summary generator was added to reconstruct the expected queue, select the latest decision per candidate, verify completeness, and produce JSON and Markdown reports.

docs.title: 2026-07-28 — Baseline review completed
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by 130 final candidate decisions and generated reports.

All 130 candidates were reviewed. Only 37 of 123 periodic detector locks were correct, corresponding to 30.1% checkpoint correctness. Eighty-two candidates were classified as station false locks. Both blue sessions and od_white_1 had zero correct periodic detector locks.

The result disproved the assumption that near-complete output coverage meant reliable tracking. It also showed that confidence thresholding was not a useful single fix: station false locks had a higher mean confidence than correct locks. The single-reference configuration was therefore rejected for unchanged live transfer.

Repeated navigation had produced 304 append-only rows for 130 unique candidates. The history was preserved, latest-decision semantics were tested, and the UI was changed to disable an unchanged save.

docs.title: 2026-07-28 — Supervisor scope decision and scientific journal
docs.text:
Evidence level: supervisor meeting record and documentation files.

The supervisor requested continuous documentation of activities, mistakes, solutions, and scientifically justified method choices. The technical scope was narrowed to completing FTS detection and tracking before other tracked objects or detailed statistics.

The next active milestone is a verified one-class fts ground-truth dataset. It must contain positive and negative station-only frames from all six videos, use video/segment-separated splits, and be manually checked before detector training or comparison begins.

docs.title: 2026-08-04 — Frozen tracker selection and six-route Replay
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by commit 4e745d7, locked evaluation artifacts, the six published Replay trajectories, and the 2026-08-04 journal.

The locked validation-first comparison selected YOLO11n + CSRT over YOLO11n + ByteTrack for the present one-object FTS task. On the locked temporal test, CSRT recorded 144 TP, 0 FP, and 0 FN at the sampled truth points, while ByteTrack recorded 88 TP, 0 FP, and 56 FN. The conclusion is limited to the fixed dataset and protocol.

All six native route videos were published to the FastAPI Replay interface. Native MP4 playback, compact synchronized overlays, FTS-only station events, journey state, and Live transfer were implemented. Physical Live route validation remained pending because the operator was away from the test room.

docs.title: 2026-08-05 — Visual-loss and physical-station semantics separated
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by commit eecf202, 126 passing tests, calibrated zone configuration, and the 2026-08-05 journal.

Stale CSRT predictions were limited to one second without detector confirmation, and explicit LOST observations were introduced. Station occupancy no longer ends because the FTS moves inside a station or becomes temporarily invisible. A departure requires sustained detected movement outside the station envelope; one noisy outside point followed by visual loss is insufficient. The CHRG service polygon was corrected for the fixed camera geometry.

docs.title: 2026-08-06 — OSF operational digital twin integrated
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by commit 7e425f9, browser checks, 126 passing tests, and the 2026-08-06 journal.

An 800×600 OSF operational view was added beside the calibrated Tracking map. It uses authorized ORBIS logos, station pictograms, intersections, and AGV graphics with recorded source revision. Camera-space FTS evidence is projected onto the operational route for Live and Replay, while the original Tracking view remains the engineering source for calibration inspection. Operational module state and future MQTT state remain conceptually separate from CV visual evidence.

docs.title: 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-12 — Workpiece feasibility established
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by commit 0ff826d, the WP-1 protocol, append-only annotations, and the observability report.

A separate workpiece study was opened without changing the validated FTS pipeline. Red, blue, and white _1 recordings were assigned to development; the corresponding _2 recordings were sealed for later evaluation. A content-blind 36-frame audit was prepared and the dashboard was extended for native-resolution, multi-piece annotation with per-piece evidence.

All 36 frames were reviewed. The final evidence contains 717 frame-level observations and represents all three colours, on-FTS transport, and station/handover contexts. WP-1 therefore passed its human-observability gate. This does not establish detector or tracking accuracy: the sample is dominated by static background pieces and contains no explicit negative frames.

The study advanced to WP-2. Fourteen 12-second candidate windows were proposed from the three _1 recordings with checksum-verified 15 FPS review clips and one-second progression sheets. The proposal covers all colours and hypothesised transport, station, handover, occlusion, empty-FTS, and background-negative conditions. These hypotheses still require human acceptance before the sequence set is frozen. Detector comparison remains deferred and _2 sources remain sealed.

docs.title: 2026-08-14 — Workpiece temporal windows human-reviewed and frozen
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by the checksum-bound WP-2 review configuration and the sequence-review report.

Human review accepted all 14 development windows without changing their 12-second boundaries. The clips provide visible transport, station, handover, occlusion, and empty-FTS evidence across red, blue, and white workpieces. The review corrected the preliminary proposal: all three supposed background negatives contain active DPS workpiece handling. The windows are frozen for 5 FPS annotation, but separate verified background negatives are still required. No _2 source was opened.

The checksum-bound 5 FPS queue was then generated from those frozen _1 windows: 840 native-resolution frames, with exactly 60 half-open samples per window. A dedicated append-only browser workflow was validated for drawing, moving, resizing, explicit copy-forward review, ambiguity rationale, and reload persistence. Human frame annotation remains pending, and the missing verified background-negative evidence continues to block WP-2 completion.

docs.title: 2026-08-20 — WP-2 development-frame annotation completed
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by the evidence-bound temporal summary, 840 latest frame decisions, the append-only decision log, and the temporal annotation report.

The first human pass completed all 840 prepared frames across the 14 frozen development sequences. The authoritative projection contains 16,835 visible frame-level instances and 281 temporary sequence-scoped identities. The append-only history contains 1,150 decisions, retaining 310 superseded rows as correction evidence. Every prepared frame has a decision and none remains pending.

This closes the development-frame annotation completeness sub-gate only. Every prepared frame contains at least one visible workpiece, so the required background-negative evidence is still absent. The held-out protocol and its future second review also remain pending; _2 sources remain sealed and detector comparison has not started.

Later the same day, 30 fixed 640×540 spatial proposals were generated from the existing checksum-bound _1 JPEGs and authoritative boxes, without decoding source video. Human review completed all 30; every authoritative decision is verified_negative, with ten crops per development session and six per configured region. The spatial negative screening gate passed. The evidence is limited to crops from nine source frames and cannot be reported as full-frame absence. The development ground-truth sub-gate is complete; _2 remains sealed until the held-out annotation protocol and detector candidates are locked.

The held-out protocol was then frozen without reading _2 media. It defines three duration-normalized 12-second windows per sealed source, producing 540 future 5 FPS frames, and fixes annotation, independent second review, prediction-first blinding, metrics, matching, and acceptance rules. This closes WP-2 but does not authorize sealed release. Detector and tracker candidates must be developed and locked on _1 evidence first, then a separate explicit release record is required. WP-3 became active.

docs.title: 2026-08-21 to 2026-08-22 — WP-3 detector comparison completed
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by locked configurations, training/checkpoint hashes, raw validation predictions, class-aware metrics, and visual error-review artifacts.

A static HSV/shape baseline and a supervised YOLO11n candidate were compared on the same sequence-grouped _1 evidence. The classical method failed with macro F1 0.0819. YOLO11n training ran on CPU because no CUDA-capable NVIDIA device was available. An interruption during epoch 16 was recorded and resumed from the preserved checkpoint without changing data or parameters. Patience-based early stopping ended training after epoch 37; the best checkpoint was epoch 25.

The frozen custom evaluator selected confidence 0.20 and measured macro F1 0.9205, overall recall 0.9167, AP50 0.9411, and per-colour recall above 0.89. All 15 validation spatial-negative crops remained prediction-free. Review of the ten largest repeated unmatched-prediction clusters found visible inventory and localization disagreement rather than station-hardware confusers. However, station-context recall was only 78/144 and remains a documented tracking risk.

The supervised detector was locked for WP-4 development. This is development-selection evidence because validation also informed early stopping, checkpoint selection, and threshold selection. No _2 source was opened; sealed release remains blocked until a tracker candidate and combined release record are locked.

docs.title: 2026-08-22 — WP-4 temporary tracker selected and locked
docs.text:
Evidence level: recorded by the pre-output tracker protocol, two hashed raw prediction streams, multi-identity metrics, and the tracker candidate lock.

Greedy detector-corrected association was compared with class-aware global motion assignment on 360 prepared _1 frames containing 7,255 visible identity instances. Both passed the existing development gate. The global candidate was selected with 0.9218 temporal coverage, minimum per-colour coverage 0.9022, seven ID switches, zero simultaneous identity swaps, and 30 fragments.

The result also exposed a major limitation: static inventory dominates the aggregate, while handover, on-FTS, and station coverage are only 0.3084, 0.3000, and 0.5556. The tracker is locked according to the predeclared rule, but robust moving-workpiece tracking is not claimed. _2 remains sealed; the combined release record and explicit operator confirmation have not been provided.

docs.title: 2026-08-22 — Held-out release record prepared, not authorized
docs.text:
Evidence level: checksum-bound metadata and regression-tested access guards; no sealed media access.

The combined release record was prepared only after the detector and tracker locks existed. It binds both locks, the original held-out protocol, the frozen acceptance rules, 540-frame sampling plan, raw prediction schemas, and the rule that prediction files must be hashed before annotation begins.

The record remains blocked. No first-pass or independent second reviewer is yet assigned, explicit operator authorization has not been recorded, both candidate permission fields remain false, and no _2 source was opened.

docs.title: 2026-08-22 — Held-out release authorized and predictions sealed
docs.text:
Evidence level: authorized release record, preserved interruption record, 540-frame manifest, two hashed raw prediction streams, execution seal, and blinded-service regression tests.

Daniel Wonkam explicitly authorized the frozen one-time procedure and ORIEL was assigned as the distinct independent reviewer. The initial attempt stopped before frame extraction when OpenCV reported 30.000125 FPS for metadata rounded to 30.0 FPS. The label-free interruption was preserved. A narrow 0.01 FPS codec metadata tolerance was tested; frame indices and all analytical settings stayed unchanged.

The successful run extracted exactly 540 images from the nine predeclared windows, then generated and hashed one detector row and one tracker row per frame. No human labels existed and no pixels were displayed during prediction preparation. The prediction files are now immutable. A separate first-pass workspace exposes only checksum-bound images and Daniel's own labels; detector and tracker outputs are never serialized to annotation clients. First-pass annotation and ORIEL's independent review remain pending.

docs.title: Scientific work documentation
docs.text: This directory is the evidence-oriented research journal for the Track & Trace thesis. It records not only what was implemented, but why a method was selected, what failed, how the failure was diagnosed, and what evidence supports the next decision.

docs.title: Current research focus
docs.text: The first tracked object is the fischertechnik transport system (FTS). FTS detection and tracking must pass the offline and live acceptance gates before workpiece tracking, event reconstruction, or detailed dashboard statistics are expanded. This scope follows the supervisor feedback recorded on 2026-07-28.

docs.title: Documents
docs.text: Document Purpose Update rule SCOPE_AND_RESEARCH_QUESTIONS.md Current scope, research questions, and completion definition Change only after a justified scope decision PROJECT_HISTORY.md Reconstructed chronology from repository evidence Add dated milestones; distinguish facts from inference DECISION_REGISTER.md Method choices, alternatives, rationale, and consequences Add an entry whenever a non-trivial choice is made LESSONS_LEARNED.md Mistakes, diagnosis, correction, and transferable lesson Add after a failure is understood EXPERIMENT_REGISTER.md Index of reproducible experiments and their conclusions Add one row per formal experiment FTS_ANNOTATION_PROTOCOL.md Rules for one-class FTS boxes, negatives, difficulty, splits, and review Revise only through a documented dataset-version decision FTS_PILOT_V0.1.md Method, evidence, limitations, and next action for the 48-frame pilot Update after annotation and quality review WORKPIECE_WP1_OBSERVABILITY.md Method, results, quality checks, gate decision, and limits for WP-1 Freeze after completion; correct only through an auditable amendment daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md Daily objective, work, evidence, reflection, and next step Update after each substantive work session ../meeting_notes/ Supervisor decisions and resulting actions Add after each meeting

docs.title: Scientific writing rule
docs.text:
Start every daily entry with a brief overview that a non-specialist can read in less than a minute:

  1. What is being done?
  2. What is the goal?
  3. What are the consequences?
  4. What are the next steps?

Use one or two direct sentences for each answer. Keep implementation details, metrics and file references in the evidence sections below the overview.

Every substantive scientific claim should then answer four questions:

  1. What was the question or problem?
  2. What method was used, and why was it chosen over alternatives?
  3. What evidence was observed?
  4. What conclusion is justified, including its limitations?

Use plain, direct language. Do not inflate ordinary engineering work into a research contribution. Separate observation from interpretation, report failed attempts, and never call candidate-level checkpoint correctness “precision” or “recall.”

docs.title: Professional experiment discipline
docs.text:
Use the following gate for every substantive experiment:

  1. State one question and a falsifiable hypothesis.
  2. Define the dataset version, source split, metrics, and acceptance threshold before running the experiment.
  3. Preserve the exact configuration, command, environment, random seed where applicable, and output location.
  4. Change one meaningful factor at a time unless the experiment explicitly studies an interaction.
  5. Separate observations from interpretation and state uncertainty.
  6. Record failed or inconclusive results; do not silently discard them.
  7. Run tests and artifact-integrity checks before advancing the milestone.
  8. Commit code, tests, documentation, and interpretation as one auditable unit.

Test data must not guide training or parameter selection. Complete source recordings belong to one split only. A milestone remains open whenever an acceptance item lacks evidence, even if the demonstration appears successful.

docs.title: Daily update automation
docs.text:
Run the journal updater from the project root:

& .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scripts.update_research_journal

The command creates or refreshes today’s entry. It updates only the marked automatic evidence block and preserves all manually written reflection. In VS Code, run the task Research: Update daily journal.

The automatic block records verifiable repository facts such as the current Git revision, commits from the day, changed files, the active milestone, and formal experiment artifacts modified that day. Scientific interpretation remains a human or supervised-agent responsibility.

docs.title: Private research portal
docs.text:
The repository includes a local MkDocs Material portal as the presentation layer over this evidence. Markdown files remain authoritative; the portal does not maintain a second copy of research results.

Build the static portal with Research Portal: Build in VS Code. Start the local preview with Research Portal: Preview, then open http://127.0.0.1:8011. The generated site/ directory is excluded from Git. The briefing page can be printed or saved as a PDF for a supervisor meeting.

Install the documentation dependencies from requirements.txt, then run python -m mkdocs build --strict from the repository root. Check the portal with python -m pytest tests/test_research_portal.py tests/test_research_journal.py -q. The tests build all three languages and audit local page links, resources, translation coverage and the offline search index.

English remains the authoritative technical record. The homepage and supervisor briefing have full French and German reading editions. Dated entries and reference pages have explicitly labelled reading summaries that link to the full English originals. Edit the persistent sources under docs/translations/fr/ and docs/translations/de/, not the generated portal copies. A newly added journal entry needs both reading summaries before a strict build can succeed.

For an approved recipient, archive the contents of site/. Extract the complete ZIP before opening index.html; no Python or web server is needed. Navigation, styling and search use local assets. Fonts use installed system faces. The first build may download public JavaScript dependencies into the local privacy-plugin cache; it does not upload research text. Future recipients need no network connection to read or search the extracted journal.

The portal is private by design. Do not publish it, its shopfloor evidence, or unfinished findings without ORBIS and university approval.

docs.title: End-of-session checklist
docs.text:
• Update today’s journal entry.
  • Add or revise a decision if a method or scope changed.
  • Add a lesson if a mistake was diagnosed.
  • Register any formal experiment and link its configuration and outputs.
  • Record exact validation commands and results.
  • State the next single task under the active milestone.

docs.title: Mistakes and lessons learned
docs.text: The purpose of this register is not to assign blame. A failed approach is useful when its assumptions, evidence, and correction are documented.

docs.title: L-001 — Planning documents can become inaccurate
docs.text:
• Observed: the early backlog still described Streamlit, SQLite, YOLO, and ByteTrack while the demonstrator had moved to FastAPI, JSONL, YOLOE, and CSRT.
  • Risk: future implementation decisions could be based on an obsolete plan.
  • Correction: the FTS roadmap became the sequential source of truth, while the broad backlog was explicitly marked as containing legacy assumptions.
  • Lesson: distinguish the current implementation record from aspirational planning, and date scope changes.

docs.title: L-002 — Processing every frame can increase live latency
docs.text:
• Observed: live preview and inference accumulated delay when older frames were retained or preview images were polled through disk files.
  • Root cause: throughput-oriented buffering conflicted with the real-time requirement for a fresh view.
  • Correction: use a dedicated capture thread, a latest-frame-only buffer, stale-frame dropping, and shared-memory preview transport.
  • Lesson: live systems should measure temporal freshness, not only average processing FPS.

docs.title: L-003 — Hard-coded camera indices are not operationally robust
docs.text:
• Observed: an external camera could be connected but not reliably selected from a fixed index assumption.
  • Correction: enumerate available Windows cameras dynamically and expose them in the dashboard.
  • Lesson: hardware identity and availability are runtime configuration, not constants.

docs.title: L-004 — Output continuity was mistaken for evidence of tracking quality
docs.text:
• Observed: the baseline emitted position rows for 99.8–100.0% of sampled frames, initially suggesting stable tracking.
  • Contradicting evidence: only 37 of 123 reviewed periodic detector locks were correct.
  • Root cause: CSRT can continuously track the wrong stationary object after an incorrect detector initialization.
  • Correction: add structured human review and distinguish output coverage from semantic correctness.
  • Lesson: availability of a bounding box is not evidence that the box belongs to the intended object.

docs.title: L-005 — One visual reference did not generalise across recordings
docs.text:
• Observed: both blue recordings and od_white_1 had zero correct periodic detector locks, while the red recordings performed much better.
  • Root cause hypothesis: the single reference did not represent sufficient viewpoint, lighting, background, and appearance variation. This hypothesis requires controlled testing in Milestone 3.
  • Correction: build ground truth first, then compare multiple reference views with a dedicated one-class detector.
  • Lesson: zero-shot convenience does not remove the need for representative evaluation data.

docs.title: L-006 — Confidence was not a reliable correctness signal
docs.text:
• Observed: mean confidence was 0.1205 for correct locks and 0.1354 for station false locks.
  • Failed proposed correction: increase the confidence threshold.
  • Reason rejected: the false locks were, on average, more confident than the correct locks.
  • Lesson: inspect class-conditional score distributions before selecting a threshold.

docs.title: L-007 — An interrupted computer invalidated a runtime measurement
docs.text:
• Observed: od_blue_2 reported 0.51 effective FPS because wall-clock time included several hours while the computer slept.
  • Correction: label that value invalid and report CPU performance from the five uninterrupted runs, approximately 14–23 source FPS.
  • Lesson: preserve execution context and reject contaminated benchmark measurements rather than averaging them into a result.

docs.title: L-008 — Environment discovery can select the wrong virtual environment
docs.text:
• Observed: automated environment configuration selected a neighbouring project environment, and the editor’s Python 3.15 interpreter lacked cv2.
  • Correction: run project validation explicitly with .venv/Scripts/python.exe from this project.
  • Lesson: record and verify the exact interpreter used for every experiment and validation command.

docs.title: L-009 — Repeated review saves created noisy history
docs.text:
• Observed: 304 append-only rows represented 130 unique candidates, including 174 repeated or corrective saves.
  • Correction: preserve the valid history, summarize by latest decision, and disable saving when verdict and trimmed note are unchanged.
  • Lesson: append-only interfaces still need idempotence cues to prevent accidental duplicate user actions.

docs.title: L-010 — A review queue is not full ground truth
docs.text:
• Observed: all detector locks and flagged anomalies were reviewed, but not every source frame with an FTS bounding box.
  • Correction: report 30.1% as checkpoint correctness, not precision, recall, or full tracking accuracy.
  • Lesson: metric names must reflect the sampling and annotation protocol that produced them.

docs.title: L-011 — A frame-level audit must not assume one visible workpiece
docs.text:
• Observed: the first WP-1 interface replaced its only rectangle when a second piece was drawn, although several same- or different-colour pieces can coexist in one camera frame.
  • Risk: incomplete annotations would incorrectly treat unlabelled visible pieces as background and make later multi-object evaluation invalid.
  • Correction: store a frame status plus a persistent list of independently boxed instances, each with colour, visibility, context, and pixel dimensions.
  • Lesson: establish object multiplicity and annotation unit before freezing an interface or dataset schema.

docs.title: L-012 — Multi-instance frames must not share object-specific attributes
docs.text:
• Observed: difficulty tags and notes were initially frame-level, so marking one stacked piece as occluded appeared to mark every clear piece in that frame.
  • Risk: mixed visibility conditions would be flattened into incorrect ground truth and failure analysis could not identify the affected instance.
  • Correction: store context, difficulty tags, and notes on each visible workpiece; reserve frame-level fields for absent or ambiguous decisions.
  • Lesson: decide whether every annotation field describes the frame or one object, and bind object attributes to stable instances in the interface.

docs.title: L-013 — Static cache keys must change with frontend contracts
docs.text:
• Observed: the browser retained an older audit script after per-piece API fields changed, so the visible page and submitted payload followed different versions of the annotation contract.
  • Risk: valid-looking work could be rejected at save time without an obvious explanation to the reviewer.
  • Correction: update the JavaScript and stylesheet cache key with the contract change, and display the required reviewer identity beside Save.
  • Lesson: version static assets whenever frontend/backend contracts change; verify the script URL and submitted payload in the browser, not only unit tests.

docs.title: L-014 — Annotation propagation must remain a proposal
docs.text:
• Observed: many workpieces remain stationary between sampled frames, making complete re-annotation repetitive.
  • Risk: automatic copy-forward can preserve disappeared or moved objects and convert reviewer expectations into false ground truth.
  • Correction: copy only on explicit request from the closest earlier reviewed same-recording frame; mark every copied box amber and block save until the reviewer confirms comparison with the current frame.
  • Lesson: annotation acceleration must preserve provenance and require fresh human verification whenever evidence changes over time.

docs.title: L-015 — Arbitrary instance limits can truncate ground truth
docs.text:
• Observed: copying 20 reviewed boxes exhausted the original 20-instance limit, preventing annotation of a newly visible twenty-first workpiece.
  • Risk: valid visible objects would be omitted and later treated as background, corrupting detector ground truth.
  • Correction: remove the fixed per-frame instance-count limit while retaining semantic validation for every box and duplicate-box rejection.
  • Lesson: annotation capacity must follow observable scene content; defensive limits must not silently redefine the scientific annotation unit.

docs.title: L-016 — CSV generation and text writing must share one newline contract
docs.text:
• Observed: the ignored WP-1 manifest projection contained CR CR LF separators and blank rows after dashboard saves on Windows.
  • Root cause: csv.DictWriter emitted CR LF, then Path.write_text translated the embedded line feed again while atomically replacing the file.
  • Risk: parsers tolerated the blank rows, but the projection failed Git's whitespace check and was not byte-clean reproducible evidence.
  • Correction: write the generated CSV content through a text handle opened with newline="" and assert that saved manifests never contain CR CR LF.
  • Lesson: generate and persist CSV under one explicit newline policy; test raw bytes on the operating system that writes the artifact.

docs.title: L-017 — A dual-load clip does not imply dual-load context in every frame
docs.text:
• Observed: the replacement sequence has 30 frames with two on_fts labels; the blue object's remaining contexts include handover, station and elsewhere.
  • Risk: earlier blanket visual claims or scenario names could cause valid transfers to be overwritten merely to satisfy an expected object count.
  • Correction: prepare image-based same-reviewer QA of the full replacement sequence, preserve original labels, and require a reason for each correction.
  • Lesson: distinguish clip-level scenario coverage from frame-level context; structural checks and consistent counts cannot substitute for visual evidence.

docs.title: L-018 — A blocked evidence gate must disable the annotation workflow
docs.text:
• Observed: an HTTP 409 left the QA view blank while edit, zoom and save controls still appeared usable. A same-label re-save, not lost annotations, caused the history checksum mismatch.
  • Correction: use explicit loading, ready, empty and blocked states; clear stale images, guard pointer/keyboard/save actions and explain recovery. Label interaction mode and zoom as separate groups.
  • Lesson: test failed metadata and image loads as well as successful startup. Human-label preservation and a usable error state are both necessary; a backend rejection alone is not an adequate interface.

docs.title: L-019 — Validate rendered themes and the delivered archive, not settings alone
docs.text:
• Observed: a custom dark scheme left near-black text on a dark navy background. Directory-style URLs and an untested search worker also made prior claims about direct-file portability insufficiently supported.
  • Correction: use full native colour schemes and measure computed text and background colours. Build explicit HTML links and bundled offline search; verify an extracted archive in a standard browser with networking disabled. On Windows, a pinned JavaScript URL with a real extension avoids the asset downloader's unsupported symbolic-link path.
  • Lesson: configuration labels do not establish readable output, and a successful server preview does not establish portable offline behaviour. Keep translated summaries distinct from original technical evidence.

In parallel, I need to move from prototype development to thesis writing.

docs.title: What still needs to be done?
docs.text:
1. Record new videos that were not used for training. They should include a simple one-piece route and realistic multi-piece configurations.
  2. Select and label a representative set of frames. Consecutive duplicate frames will be avoided so that the evaluation remains useful and manageable.
  3. Compare the previous and new workpiece models on exactly the same unseen frames.
  4. Evaluate whether several pieces can be detected, tracked, and assigned to the correct station history without identity switches.
  5. Decide from this evidence whether the technical work can be closed or whether one small, targeted correction is necessary.
  6. Begin the thesis structure and write the method and completed results while the final evaluation is being prepared.
